paragraphs: HAAS Alert sells a collision prevention service that sends real-time digital alerts warning drivers about nearby emergency vehicles and roadway hazards. Its customers are fleets that work at the roadside, including tow trucks, utility vehicles, waste management trucks, school buses and snowplows.

The system is wired to a vehicle's warning light bar or master switch, so alerting begins when crews turn on their lights and stops when they turn them off. Motorists install nothing, because alerts are broadcast directly to the navigation platforms they already use. Fleets can activate the service through three primary methods, depending on their existing setup. The company says drivers get up to 30 seconds of advance warning to slow down and move over.

The company traces its start to 2015, when co-founder and CEO Cory Hohs was almost struck by an ambulance on the road. He co-founded the business with Noah Levens and Jigar Patel. Its timeline notes that the United States Department of Homeland Security awarded $1.1 million toward development for digital alerting. It also states that digital alerting was codified and funded in the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act.

quote.text: Built in America for first responders and roadside workers so everyone gets home safely.
